title: Full project review: tests C+, docs C+, data not fit for training
detail: Principal review of the whole repository. Tests graded C+ (many passed without executing solvers, data checks mixed into the unit run, the audit ledger polluted by test runs). Documentation graded C+ (stale commands, retired Markdown layer still described, mixed-language skills). Data judged NOT fit for training: grounded-paraphrase injected unstated negative premises into about 64% of the training mix; about 70% of the mix came from one templated corpus; targets were predictable from the CONTEXT block instead of the message. Consequence: no current corpus qualifies, and training stays prohibited regardless (AGENTS.md rule 3).

Results are in eval/reports/current/corpus-audit/<corpus>.json; most legacy corpora fail faithfulness or leakage checks, which confirms the review verdict.

title: Owner decision: stated / assumed / unclear wires, one keyword per line
detail: The small model reports what the message says with stated, what it adds with assumed, and an unintelligible or request-free message with unclear. One keyword per line.

title: Owner decision: no model context; string-based targets with the closed role set
detail: The formalizer input is the user message only (no shortlist, identifiers, knowledge or clock). Targets are quoted strings: a relation phrase plus roles from the closed set subject, object, recipient, location, source, destination, instrument, time, topic. The host links strings to the lexicon.

title: Owner decision: unclear = gibberish | no_request
detail: unclear has exactly two kinds: gibberish (unintelligible) and no_request (no statement and no question). Nothing else is unclear.

title: Owner decision: no model-level refusal
detail: The model never refuses; every message is formalized. What the reasoner can conclude is decided by the host, not by the model.

title: Current work: data — what is being done now and why
detail: WHY: the review found the existing corpora unfit (unstated negatives injected in ~64% of the mix, ~70% from one templated corpus, targets predictable from CONTEXT), and sop-agent-4 removes the model context altogether, so every existing corpus (sop-agent-3 targets with a CONTEXT shortlist) must be rebuilt rather than patched. WHAT: (1) mine a diversity inventory of question types, paraphrase operations, ambiguity types and reasoning depth from the cached sources, taking structure and statistics only, never text; (2) generate cases from an intermediate representation and print them as sop-agent-4 string targets, with the message as the only model input and the world, ontology and expected result kept as evaluation-only scaffolding; (3) verify every target by executing it against its world; (4) enforce quotas and split grouping so the sealed test is not answerable by template recall; (5) audit the pilot for faithfulness, diversity and leakage; (6) only then regenerate all corpora. NOT DONE: no training, no fine-tuning; data qualification is a separate gate from the owner approval required by AGENTS.md rule 3.

title: Owner decisions Q-LANG-1..7, Q-DATA-7; training waits for expanded data

title: Words-only model constructs for Q-LANG-1..7 and conventions C1-C12

DS021 sections 'Words, not operators' and 'Conventions C1-C12'; query/constraint/stated/question-types/model-guide/small-model help pages with executed examples; prompt updated; tests/model-language-words.test.mjs. Remaining failures belong to corpus regeneration (operator syntax in current corpora) and to the sealed wild suite golds.

title: formalizer-size-v1: Gemma GGUF export lost its turn tokens; first Gemma sealed numbers invalidated and rerun
detail: The first Gemma Q8_0 run parsed only 93.8% of short test rows (287 outputs lacked their first line), while HF gave 99.96% syntax on dev. Cause: the GGUF built from the transformers 5 checkpoint tokenizer save tokenized <start_of_turn>/<end_of_turn> as plain text, because the save omits added_tokens.json, special_tokens_map.json and the full tokenizer_config.json that the SentencePiece converter reads (f16 showed the same; SmolLM2's ChatML GGUF was verified correct). The checkpoint tokenizer is identical to the base (same vocabulary and special flags), so merged-best now takes its tokenizer files from the pinned base; <start_of_turn> is one token (id 105) again, and 20 of 20 sampled previously broken rows produce well-formed programs. The invalid run (short rows: tolerant 73.2%, parse 93.8%) is kept for diagnosis under eval/reports/current/formalizer-size-v1/gemma-invalid-special-tokens/ and is NOT a Gemma result. The Gemma evaluation restarts.

title: Long-message diagnosis: 0% is mostly a strict all-or-nothing metric plus real errors that grow with length; no truncation, no harness bug
detail: formalizer-v1 long_message rows (303 test; golds median 27 wires, up to 79). Truncation: none (0/303 finish=length, max 2762 of 6144 tokens, prompt+completion max 4647 of 8192 context per slot, last wire parses 303/303). Partial credit (new formalizer.wire_match, DS016 'Wire F1'), short vs long: SmolLM2-135M Q8_0 test wire F1 0.785 vs 0.589, query part right 76.6% vs 10.2%, rows >=0.9 F1 75.5% vs 1.7%, exec 78.8% vs 0%; the same model on dev (HF, selection run) 0.980 vs 0.839, rows >=0.9 97.3% vs 37.0%, exec 97.7% vs 7.8%; Haiku no-thinking sample 0.412 vs 0.618, query part 38.8% vs 23.2%, exec 46.9% vs 1.6%. With about 22 parts per row, independent parts at the short-row rate would give 2.8% exact at best (61% on dev), so exact execution on long rows is mostly an arithmetic effect. Real errors: statement recall drops from 0.78 at the first statement to 0.55 from the 11th; misses are wrong role values (1228), dropped statements (946), wrong relation phrases (765); 1322 extra statements carry values absent from the message (corrupted name copies), 131 questions turned into statements, and queries misaligned or with the wrong relation (354 of 702 missed). English long 0.69, mixed 0.56, Romanian 0.46. Golds: 15 reviewed by hand, consistent (chit-chat and errands omitted, embedded statements hoisted before queries, canonical English values in Romanian). Gemma predictions not present yet.

title: Owner: SOP Lang as translation — decisions on next research
detail: Owner frames NL->SOP as translation into a new language. Rejects a compact intermediate form (problem is not that simple: queries, compound sentences). Suspects SOP Lang may map natural language too simplistically; asks Fable for a proposal grounded in grammatical analysis: decompose compound/subordinate/conditional sentences into short simple propositions chained with $ references as a more real circuit, and build examples that way. Approves: grammar-constrained decoding experiment on existing models; fine-tuning a small translation model (Opus-MT) directly to SOP Lang and comparing with the current models (training authorized for this comparison). Defers back-translation and SOP-only pretraining. Major results and observations must be documented on the site with links.

title: Clause decomposition proposal: short wires chained with $ (PROPOSED)
detail: Read-only language-design review answering the owner's 'analiza frazei' idea. Diagnosis: wild rows with subordinate clauses score proposition F1 0.41 vs 0.63; golds flatten clauses into strings, drop because/after/so links, and make 'if' clauses global. Proposal: 'clause TYPE $id' (cause, condition, concession, purpose, before, after, during) and '$id' as a role value (event of a statement or answers of an earlier query); revisits DS021's ban on $ in stated/assumed. Basis: clause analysis + PDTB relations + flat neo-Davidsonian propositions + QDMR-style back-references. Validation: paired experiment eval-clause-decomposition-v1 (flat vs chained, two SmolLM2-135M runs; needs approval). Owner decisions L1–L6 appended to questions.md. No code, spec, dataset or training change.

title: Owner decisions D1-D6 and L1-L6
detail: D1: do not burden the small model with translation; it must recognize intent and normalize the language coherently (Romanian content words passed through in a normalized form); symbolic dictionary-based normalization/translation happens in the host before reasoning. Supersedes the English-canonical rule for content words (Q-DATA-6). D2: yes to LLM-authored diversification, systematically, via a Haiku agent, with verification. D3: freeze v1 sealed suites; account for the D1 change. D4: cap long messages and add a medium family. D5: approve training experiments one by one; the full 1-2 week series is too long and the learning goals must be clear. D6: align the wild suite to current conventions. L1: yes - split compound sentences into short linked propositions; no whole clauses stuffed into strings. L2: leaning to conjunction keywords (because/if/...), possibly settled by experiment. L3: A ( chaining). L4: A (not_checked). L5: A. L6: A (approve the paired clause-decomposition experiment).

title: Owner idea: honest partial formalization with unparsed spans and symbolic repair
detail: Owner: instead of complaining and giving up, the small model should formalize what it understood and return the parts it did not understand in special wires; symbolic heuristics (with context/history) then repair what they can. Measured on wild: fine-tuned models give up entirely on 1.9-9.3% of content rows (360M 13/676, 135M 25/676, Gemma 63/676), but silently invent more often (about 15% corrupted names, 8% invented values). Design: model-authored 'unparsed' wire (verbatim span, optional near $id and hint), host repair step (date/number/money parsers, name recognizer, bilingual/synonym lexicon, conversation history), targeted clarification per unresolved span, honesty metric. Added to language v2.

title: Proofreader in front of the symbolic path: prove on English first, no training

Conditions R, P-coedit (jbochi/coedit-small), P-gec (Unbabel/gec-t5_small), H (Haiku no-thinking rewrite), Hbest (4 Haiku rewrites, the rules pick the one with an admitted SOP and fewest unparsed spans; no gold), O (oracle simple text). Names, quotes and numbers masked symbolically before every rewriter. Futility/broken stops only. Dev pilot (n=100 tolerant exec): R 46, P-coedit 46, P-gec 50, H 41, Hbest 39, O 60.

OOD tolerant exec R 20.6 / P-coedit 20.6 / P-gec 20.9 / H 24.0 (+3.5 [-0.7,+7.9]) / Hbest 23.0 / O 38.7 (+18.1 [+13.1,+23.5]); test R 35.1 / P-gec 36.1 / H 35.8 / Hbest 29.8 (-5.3) / O 55.8 (+20.7); wild prop F1 R 0.605 / P 0.602-0.610 / H 0.592 / O 0.766, but H raises wild decision +9.0 [+4.3,+13.7] and accepted +4.0 [0,+8]. Hbest (fewest unparsed) parses better (unparsed 7-26%) but is less correct. Names kept 95-100% (P), 88-93% (H). Reproducibility P 100/100, H 55/100. Distilling H/Hbest not worth training; only an IR-rendered oracle-style target shows a large gain. Romanian stage not run.

title: baseline-ud-rules-v1 done: Stanza + UD rules shipped as the chat formalizer 'Stanza + rules (symbolic baseline)'

We have not understood the symbolic translation well enough and keep running to LLMs. Evaluate in layers: first whether Stanza's analysis is correct (LLM only as validator), then our UD->SOP translation on correct parses, then whether wrong parses can be saved by rewrites into a form that parses correctly; collect those as candidates for a language-regularization model. Use a Fable agent to derive new rules or SOP Lang extensions from translation failures.

New corpus datasets/proofing (owner name: dataset_proofing), collected locally by running Stanza over the formalizer-v1 train/dev rows, finding parse failures, and running small proofreading LLM candidates with a no-regression check. detail: Owner: the small LLM never writes SOP; it only rewrites English text so SymbolicLM parses it well. Flow: SymbolicLM translates Romanian words to English (rough but syntactically sane), the small LLM proofreads the English (gated by a SymbolicLM uncertainty signal if one proves reliable, otherwise always), then SymbolicLM parses and emits SOP Lang. The proofing dataset is English text to English text; the gold-SOP match is only the arbiter.

title: Diverse-dev evaluation: proofreader gain is real but smaller than on generator suites, unlike the wild-suite null
detail: eval-proofreader-diverse-dev-v1, full 415 EN rows (stopped 'complete', all 3 stages run). no_rewrite strict 33.49%. gemma_always_on 36.39%, delta +2.89pp [0.99,5.15] (CI excludes 0, break 0.72%, gained 13/lost 1) -- comparable in size to formalizer-ood-v1's +2.84pp, decisively smaller than formalizer-v1's +6.67pp, but NOT null like formalizer-wild-v1's -1pp [-3,0]. gemma_gate_no_spacy 35.42%, delta +1.93pp [0.48,3.92] (break 0%). qwen_proof (untrained reference) 34.46%, delta +0.96pp [-0.96,3.21] -- CI includes 0, not significant, break 2.88% (H3 confirmed: untrained reference does not clearly help here). Interpretation: the proofreader DOES generalize partially to Haiku-diversified paraphrases of formalizer-v1 content (casual register, typos, code-switched proper nouns), which still share underlying entities/structure with the generator corpus, but the gain is smaller than on pure generator-distribution suites and much larger than on formalizer-wild-v1's fully independently-authored text -- consistent with a style-overfitting explanation that is partial, not total. Cost: $3.9075 (diversify batch only; teacher calls for the v2 build are separate, tracked in datasets/proofing-diverse-dev/teacher-ledger.json).

detail: Owner decision 2026-09-30. The first level of datasets/ holds only three folders, with the same names on the audit page. (1) bad_english: mixed Romanian/English, Romanian, spelling and grammar problems; material to evaluate or fine-tune LanguageProofingLLM. (2) symbolic_english: correct English that SymbolicLM analyses correctly; it shows SymbolicLM's grammatical analysis and serves as the regression suite when SymbolicLM, Stanza or the engine changes, and as seed forms for neuro_english targets. (3) neuro_english: grammatically correct English that SymbolicLM does not analyse correctly; fine-tuning material for SymbolicProofingLLM. Names: SymbolicProofingLLM is the small fine-tuned LLM that rewrites correct English into the limited English SymbolicLM understands, keeping the meaning. LanguageProofingLLM is a standard or separately fine-tuned LLM that turns bad English, Romanian and mixed text into acceptable English; ideally it is a decent translation model. Priority: extend SymbolicLM with rules and repairs first; rewriting covers only what rules cannot fix. For now, verify the grammatical analysis with a calibrated teacher LLM; SOP Lang generation is a later stage, once the small LLM reaches about 99% transfer into forms SymbolicLM handles. Base models must run at 30-40 tokens/s on a normal laptop CPU. Rename everything consistently in docs, server and DS. Sonnet sub-agents do the work; Opus verifies and corrects.

Decision (orchestrator, following the owner's DeepSeek-first rule): future gating of symbolic_english uses identical trees AND DeepSeek a/c good, with a 5% Fable audit on real data. title: Incident: symbolic/neuro split used SOP match instead of the grammatical analysis
detail: The owner defined symbolic_english as 'correct English that SymbolicLM analyses correctly (and the analysis is correct)'. The builders implemented it with a proxy: a row with a gold SOP entered symbolic_english only if SymbolicLM produced that SOP. As a result, about 3,700 rows whose analysis is probably correct but whose SOP translation fails (rules 1,926, gold conventions 1,819) sit in neuro_english, and SymbolicProofingLLM iteration 1 and the neuro oracle trained or selected on them. Found by the owner's question on 2026-09-30 night. Fix: re-split symbolic/neuro on the analysis layer (default/accurate trees identical AND DeepSeek judge a and c good), keep the SOP fields as information for the later layer, rebuild the SymbolicProofingLLM pairs on the new split, and treat iteration 1 as a pilot on the old split. Records of affected experiments get a deviation note.

title: Owner: good enough first; graded severity, zero catastrophic interpretations, never no interpretation
detail: Owner 2026-10-01: first phase = a good-enough system with clear room for improvement. Perfection is not the goal (large LLMs lose nuances too; users rephrase). What matters: no catastrophic interpretation (opposite meaning, role swap, wrong entity, negation flip) and never 'no interpretation' when a clear one exists: a fallback cascade (rewrite, sampled rewrites, alternative paraphraser, symbolic simplification, clarification) must produce some interpretation. Evaluation adds graded severity (S0 equivalent, S1 nuance, S2 partial, S3 wrong but noticeable, S4 catastrophic, NONE) next to pass/fail.

title: Owner: EmotionDetectionSystem as a separate, switchable component that emits pragmatic SOP circuits to the reasoner
detail: Owner 2026-10-01: add EmotionDetectionSystem, which can be enabled or disabled and has pluggable strategies (symbolic lexicons and patterns, small neural classifiers, an LLM slot for later). It emits host-generated SOP Lang circuits (a pragmatic wire: kind, score, span, source) that the reasoner uses as advisory, subjective signals to regulate itself (thinking level, strategy, clarification, short courtesy replies). Leftover unparsed spans (greetings, politeness, interjections, profanity, urgency, hedges, discourse markers, tags) are classified by pragmatic role instead of staying unparsed, and the chat shows which spans were classified. Best speed/quality compromise; not 100% verifiable by design.

title: Reasoning proposal: current strategies analysed
detail: Read reasoning/ and DS006/DS013. Today there are exactly two strategies, 'reference' (bounded JavaScript only: finite function-free Horn with explicit negation as independent evidence, no negation-as-failure, finite-domain integer constraints by enumeration, plus small JS controllers for abduce/diagnose/plan/simulate/induce) and 'advanced' (the same JS controllers, plus SWI-Prolog for point-in-time Horn and Z3 for integer constraints and optimisation when present). Prolog and Z3 are thin adapters: Prolog only recomputes the closure, JS rebuilds the proof; Z3 is not a Horn backend at all. So the 'JS-only' strategy is a useful reference oracle but has no aggregation, no negation as failure, no defaults, no tabling or magic sets, and no budget-aware partial answers beyond maxNodes/timeout flags. Private SWI 9.0.4 and Z3 4.15.8 binaries already exist under tools/.solvers (not installed by me). Next: digest the four zips and advanced_research.md in parallel.

title: Reasoning proposal: soplab-v0.4.0 analysed
detail: soplab is a dependency-free Node research harness whose core idea is one shared IR: a relation of variable bindings with evidence. Its 8 block types are claim, all, any, reduce, rule, goal, transition (planning operator) and assumption (abducible). Semantics: four-valued signed evidence (unknown, supported, refuted, conflicting) with no explosion, NOT = explicit negative evidence versus NONE = absence (stratified negation as failure), aggregates through reduce, proof DAGs. Measured: semi-naive delta needs 9365 candidate rows against 21217 for naive with identical answers (results/baseline.json); a specialised graph wire visits 87 edges against 18885 candidate rows for recursive rules, same 44 answers (results/graph-wire-vs-rules.txt). It runs as plain Node (23 of 23 tests pass). Lacks epistemic status, roles, budgets, time. Next: sop-r, E10 and VRC digests, then draft the unified wire set.

title: Reasoning proposal: sop_reasoner_e10 analysed
detail: E10 is a bottom-up Datalog engine (stratified negation, SCC scheduling, semi-naive evaluation, hash indexes, greedy joins, magic-set demand rewriting), not Prolog-like and never compared with SWI or another Datalog engine; it is validated against an independent nested-loop reference evaluator and hand-written SQLite SQL. Main benchmark: 220 complete exactly-correct runs, 23 explicit INCOMPLETE, 9 not applicable, zero wrong answers among complete runs. Key lesson for the interface: a budget overrun is reported INCOMPLETE and is never read as a negative answer. Its dreaming idea (offline consolidation of verified skills, then a frozen deployment plan used online) cut probes from 300001 (incomplete) to 167 on a 106,800-fact world. Neural join-order ranker only ties the analytical heuristic. Runs as plain Node (202 of 202 tests pass). Next: sop-r, VRC and the 48-direction catalogue.

title: Reasoning proposal: sop-r analysed
detail: sop-r is the experiment closest to the intended product loop: a coding LLM reads a handbook and compiles it into SOP wires (fact, rule, constraint, method for knowledge; find, group, assume, plan, check, answer for queries), and a Node engine answers. Pilot: 3 independent Sonnet compilations answered 215 of 216 compound what-if answers correctly (the one miss was a query-writing error with set on a directional relation), and an LLM reading the text directly scored 144 of 144, so the pilot shows the chain works but not that it beats a long-context LLM. Good ideas to reuse: overrides and supersedes for defaults and updates, stratified unless, aggregates through named views, constraints that report violations with a message, methods with require/forbid giving a reason when blocked, hypothetical worlds, why-trees, vocabulary-drift lint. Scale: a what-if world costs 30.9 ms against 29,424.5 ms naive at 100k entities. Weaknesses: only 3-term statements, no time, no explicit negation, the compiler saw the vocabulary. Next: VRC and the 48-direction catalogue.

title: Reasoning proposal: vrc03r and advanced_research.md analysed
detail: VRC v0.3 is a zero-dependency Node package with four parts: a finite Datalog-like relational reasoner (semi-naive, slicing, a narrow reachability template), an exact-rational compiler that compresses planning states into a certified smaller encoding, a bounded BFS planner over compressed states, and a registry of certified artefacts with offline dreaming. Honest findings: the SWI-Prolog comparison was never run (all 9 cases SKIPPED, swipl missing), so there are no parity numbers; 'million rules' is really one million background facts with about 1,003 rules; the huge graph speed-ups (17x to 1382x) come from a demand-directed reachability template, not from VRC; the VRC-specific gains are 39.5x (energy world, 68,726 to 6,313 states) and 1719.7x (product world) with a 0.96x negative control; validation is its own differential testing (4,764 worlds, 14,288 runs, 0 differences, plus 160 planning worlds). Budget overrun is a distinct BUDGET status, never a negative answer. Important correction: advanced_research.md is not a catalogue of alternative reasoning strategies; its 48 cards R01 to R48 are research and verification directions for VRC itself, and top-down tabling, ASP or SAT/SMT appear only as comparators, so the proposal must add a strategy-family comparison plan of its own. Next: draft the unified wire set and the validator.

detail: Design decision after reading all sources: keep the existing ChatSOP wire conventions (@id type, two-space fields, whitespace terms, all/any/end) and unify around a small CORE that every strategy can consume (fact, rule with not = explicit negation and absent = negation as failure over a declared closed predicate, compare, compute, order, aggregate, constraint, action, goal, hypothesis, policy) plus SUGAR that desugars into the core (default with except and priority becomes stratified NAF rules; integrity becomes a violation-deriving rule) plus procedure knowledge (method). Query side stays the small-model surface (query, stated, constraint) with three new modes: why_not, plan, abduce. Strategies declare which core features they support; a strategy that cannot express a wire must say not expressible, never drop it. Written so far: a standalone validator (eval/smoke-reasoning/validator.mjs, 20 deliberately invalid circuits all rejected with the expected error code) and 35 smoke cases that all validate. Next: harness and adapters (reference JS, Prolog, Z3 through the product runtime; soplab from the unpacked zip), then the proposal text.

title: Reasoning smoke harness run: per-strategy results
detail: 36 smoke cases and a standalone validator now exist in eval/smoke-reasoning/. The harness runs one adapter per strategy (the owner asked for separate strategies, not 'advanced'): js-reference passes 26 of the 26 cases it can express (10 not expressible), prolog-swi 19 of 19 (17 not expressible: it is only a point-in-time Horn closure), z3-lia 3 of 3 (integer constraints only), and two Datalog engines wired read-only from the zips: datalog-e10 19 of 19 (17 not expressible) and datalog-soplab 25 of 26 (the one failure is real: its abduction returns one cheapest explanation, not all minimal ones). Nine more strategies are planned stubs. Plain-language reading: everything every engine can state, it answers correctly; the interesting part is the not-expressible map, which shows exactly which wires each engine lacks (negation as failure, aggregates, defaults, methods, why-not, epistemic status are missing from today's product engines). Also found: the current runtime reports an overrun as status unknown with complete false, which the harness has to translate to budget_exhausted; the proposal makes that a first-class status. Next: write the proposal, including the owner's new section on routing problems to strategies.

title: Reasoning proposal: retrieval at scale added (memory to engine)
detail: Owner asked how the engine gets the right wires when memory holds millions or billions. Added to the smoke suite three cases with a generated distractor memory (about 9,300, 3,900 and 2,000 stored wires; needed wires 5, 4 and 14) and a retrieval layer in the harness: a symbol-driven slice (rule-dependency radius, constant hops, per-predicate cap), a widening loop with targeted or blind policy, and the rule that negation as failure, aggregates, count and every are only accepted over fully retrieved predicates. Results: targeted widening fetched 5 wires of 9,305 (3 steps), 4 of 3,904 (2 steps) and 9 of 2,009 (2 steps) with 100% recall of the needed wires; fetching whole predicates is 504 and 2,009 wires, and the current product parser refuses 5,005 wires (limit 2,048). With the guard disabled, all three cases give wrong answers (for the negation case, two blocked nodes are reported open). Smoke totals now (39 cases): js-reference 28/28, prolog-swi 21/21, z3-lia 3/3, datalog-e10 22/22, datalog-soplab 28/29. Observed in the HTTP chat of world-v1: 'Is Paris in France?' ends in 'Which entity do you mean by France?' (located_in role location place). title: Q-LANG-10 option A implemented: candidate $id, mode effect, abduce over candidates, if $r on session rules
detail: Owner decision 2026-10-03. query takes candidate $id (1-8, modes effect/abduce; a supposed stated or a session rule/default in force only in that query's runs, never stored). mode effect classifies each candidate establishes/blocks/contradicts/no_effect/inconsistent against a ground claim (packet effects); abduce over candidates returns minimal consistent sets plus necessary; if $r may suppose a session rule. Validator: candidate_needs_mode, effect_needs_ground_claim, candidate_target, candidate_also_if, candidate_limit (+ candidate_temporal_link on the model surface); same five on the knowledge surface. js-reference oracle runs it; every other engine refuses (not_expressible); router R1 sends it to the oracle. Rendering from conversation-v1 lines. Docs DS004/DS014/DS006, wire_types, query.html, query-modes.html (logic 171/91/541 executed). Battery: L1 1341/1341, L2 full 2492 programs, 0 losses, 0 failures, ledger refreshed; L3 +5 catalog messages (formalizer not wired yet: needs a fol-v3 role-prompt extension for argument questions). Offline regression 104/360, 0 lost.

Index per day; tinyagent lambdas|call|calls list/show/tree/search/prune; GET /v1/calls. Plan cache migrated to .tinyagent/lambdas.
